title: ‘Artificial’ First Reactions: Luca Guadagnino’s OpenAI Drama is ‘Provocative,’ ‘Downright Horrifying’ and His ‘Best Film in a Decade’
key_facts: Luca Guadagnino's 'Artificial' premiered at the New York Film Festival on Monday night (5 Oct 2026); early reviews from the film press call the Sam Altman-centred movie 'provocative', a 'visceral corporate drama' and the director's 'best film in a decade'.

Next Best Picture's Matt Neglia wrote it is 'as entertaining as it is terrifying' and praised Andrew Garfield's performance as Altman; Variety's Clayton Davis called it Guadagnino's best film in a decade and critic Eric Kohn a 'pitch-perfect dark comedy'.

The film is set during Altman's firing and rehiring as OpenAI chief executive in 2023; Garfield plays Altman, Yura Borisov plays Ilya Sutskever, Monica Barbaro plays Mira Murati, Ike Barinholtz plays Elon Musk and Mark Rylance plays Geoffrey Hinton.

In June, Neon closed a deal to complete the $40 million film after Amazon MGM Studios dropped the project months earlier, after the company signed a major partnership with OpenAI including a $50 billion investment.
Guadagnino told Vulture he was not 'afraid' of Altman's response and said people with a lot of power must be responsible for the community.
Altman told Vanity Fair that Garfield 'did walk like me' when he saw the production filming near his house, and called it very strange.
Neon's awards campaign will put Garfield and Rylance in the supporting actor category, Borisov in lead actor and Barbaro in supporting actress.
The film opens in theatres on Christmas Day from Neon; the script is by Simon Rich.
